title: sp architects adapts antalya expo grounds for COP31
summary:
SP ARCHITECTS REWORKS EXPO 2016 FOR COP31 IN ANTALYAAntalya’s former EXPO 2016 site has taken on a second assignment.
As COP31 runs in the Turkish city from November 9 to 20, SP Architects has transformed the 875,117-square-meter horticultural exhibition grounds in Aksu into a conference campus for diplomats, scientists, civil society and visitors.
the former Expo grounds have been transformedMODULAR STRUCTURES GIVE COP31 A LIFE BEYOND THE SUMMITThroughout the complex, SP Architects has sought to balance the demanding requirements of an international diplomatic event with a more adaptable architectural framework.
New permanent and temporary structures are integrated into the existing grounds, with modular and reusable components intended to limit unnecessary construction.
For SP Architects, the redevelopment represents an investment in the city’s future rather than a temporary backdrop for international diplomacy.

title: Bluetongue virus confirmed on County Down farm
summary:
The first case of Bluetongue in Northern Ireland this season has been confirmed on a farm in Kilkeel, County Down.
Officials from the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (Daera) said the virus had been detected in three sheep.
There will be no additional movement restrictions or disease control zones, because the virus has been present in Northern Ireland since November 2025.
The minister, Andrew Muir, said the discovery of the virus was "disappointing but not unexpected", given the spread of the disease in Great Britain and Ireland.
The Chief Veterinary Officer, Brian Dooher, urged local farmers to be alert to any symptoms in their livestock.

title: New Orleans port sues owners of tanker involved in Mississippi crash

New Orleans port sues owners of tanker involved in Mississippi crashtoggle caption i Gerald Herbert/APNew Orleans port officials filed a lawsuit against the owner and operator of the tanker that crashed into a docked cruise ship in the Mississippi River on Friday.
The Board of Commissioners of the Port of New Orleans is seeking at least $1 million in damages from people connected to the tanker, which is called Atlantic Asphalt.
The lawsuit also states that the port expects to incur additional costs, including clean-up, surveys, repair, replacement and salvage costs.
On Friday, port officials requested the tanker be seized and sold to cover costs of the damage.

title: Mexico’s Parque del Jaguar protects jaguars with 18-kilometre limestone wall
summary:
Mexican studio Colectivo C733 has created an 18-kilometre-long limestone wall that allows wildlife to pass through while protecting more than 1,000 hectares of forest at Parque del Jaguar in Tulum, Mexico.
The park occupies a coastal territory containing tropical forest, mangroves, underground rivers and karstic geology, as well as the ancient Mayan archaeological site of Tulum.
At its perimeter, the studio added an 18-kilometre dry-stacked limestone wall, known locally as a tecorral, informed by traditional Mayan stone boundaries.
“By designing how the territory is revealed, inhabited, and understood over time, Parque del Jaguar shifts architecture from a static intervention to an evolving framework that connects environment, culture, and collective awareness,” Colectivo C733 said.
Founded in 2019, Colectivo C733 brings together the practices of Gabriela Carrillo, Carlos Facio, José Amozurrutia, Eric Valdez and Israel Espín to work on public architecture and urban infrastructure across Mexico.

title: Indonesian president apologises to Singapore, Malaysia for wildfire haze
summary:
⁠Indonesian President ⁠Prabowo Subianto has apologised to Singapore and Malaysia ⁠for the transboundary haze due to months-long wildfires.
The haze travelled to Malaysia and to Singapore.
Previously, an Indonesian official faced criticism after claiming the country’s forests supply oxygen to Malaysia and Singapore despite recurring haze from wildfires.
Prabowo’s remarks came as the problem of transboundary haze has begun to disappear.
On Thursday, the ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) issued a “no transboundary smoke haze” notice for southern parts of Southeast Asia, the Jakarta Post reported.
